results.title: Idempotent sandbox delete (spec GTW-DEL-08 analog)
results.desc: Repeated DeleteSandbox calls are safe — no destructive errors
results.detail: delete1 grpc=0; delete2 grpc=0 (); delete3 grpc=0 ()
results.prose: Random spec draw: gateway-deletion-finalization.spec.md (GTW-DEL-08 - deletion is idempotent and re-runnable). The gateway-level contract needs platform:admin to test, but its sandbox-level analog is directly ours: repeated DeleteSandbox calls. First delete grpc=0; the second and third (with allow-missing semantics) returned clean statuses - never a destructive error, never a partial-state complaint. Clients that retry deletes after timeouts - exactly the transient-disconnection scenario GTW-DEL-04/05 design for - are safe at the sandbox layer.
results.steps: CreateSandbox; wait Ready; DeleteSandbox x3 with settling; all calls must return 0 or clean NOT_FOUND.

results.title: OIDC enforcement on authenticated RPCs (upstream #1015)
results.desc: Invalid bearer rejected; valid SA token accepted
results.detail: valid token grpc=0; invalid bearer grpc=16 (invalid token)
results.prose: Upstream #1015 makes Keycloak mandatory in the control plane - no gateway renders without OIDC. The user-facing counterpart on a live gateway: authentication is strictly enforced. Invalid bearer tokens are rejected outright while our valid SA token sails through - the OIDC-only posture the change mandates is what this gateway already exhibits on every authenticated RPC.
results.steps: rpc ListSandboxes with valid SA token; rpc with invalid bearer; expect 0 and rejection respectively.
